newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hundreds attend burials of Australian athletes.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds attend burials of Australian athletes.

text.p: Two Australian athletes killed when a bridge collapsed at an international Jewish sports festival were buried in Sydney on Friday after services attended by hundreds of people.
About 500 people attended the traditional Jewish burial ceremony for Greg Small, a 37-year-old tenpin bowler killed on Monday when a temporary bridge fell into a river near Tel Aviv.
One unidentified mourner told reporters the congregation "just broke up in tears" when Small's wife Suzanne, who received minor injuries in the collapse, arrived.
Shmuel Moyal, Israel's ambassador to Australia, read a message from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at Small's service.
Part of Netanyahu's message said: "My words will not comfort you, but the whole house of Israel grieves and mourns with you".
An Israeli consular official read the same message at a separate funeral for Yetty Bennett, 50, another member of Australia's tenpin bowling team.
Rabbi Jordan Cohen told the gathering that Bennett, the mother of three children, had been visiting Israel for the first time.
Her partner, Frank Gainsler, was among seven other Australians critically injured in the bridge collapse.

"We are simply devastated by this tragedy," Cohen said. The bridge leading to the Ramat Gan stadium near Tel Aviv collapsed as the 370-strong Australian contingent prepared to enter the stadium for the opening ceremony of the 51-nation Maccabiah Games, nicknamed the "Jewish Olympics".
Over 40 members of the Australian delegation were injured in the collapse. Israel has established a commission to probe the bridge collapse.
